subtopics.title: Complexities, Rules & Formulas Cheat-Sheet
subtopics.subtitle: Complexities, normal forms, transaction rules, scheduling, memory and disk formulas

concepts.text: This chapter spans three subjects — data structures and algorithms, databases, and operating systems — and each is tested through a small set of complexities, definitions and formulas. The tables below collect them in syllabus order. Use them for last-minute revision; every entry is explained with worked examples in its subtopic.

concepts.latex: f(n) = O(g(n)) \iff \exists\, c, n_0:\ f(n) \le c\,g(n)\ \forall n \ge n_0
concepts.plainText: Big-O: f is bounded above by c·g for all n ≥ n₀ (Ω bounds below, Θ both)

rows: linear search, one pass over a list
merge sort, heap sort, average quick sort
bubble, selection, insertion sort; nested loops
insert at head O(1), search O(n)
search O(h): O(log n) balanced, O(n) skewed

concepts.latex: \text{Binary tree of height } h:\ \le 2^{h+1} - 1 \text{ nodes};\qquad n_0 = n_2 + 1
concepts.plainText: A binary tree of height h has at most 2^(h+1) − 1 nodes; leaves = nodes of degree 2 + 1

items: Preorder: root, left, right. Inorder: left, root, right (sorted for a BST). Postorder: left, right, root (used to delete a tree).
Infix → postfix uses an operator stack: pop operators of higher or equal precedence before pushing; parentheses force grouping.
Postfix evaluation uses an operand stack: push operands, pop two for each operator, push the result.

rows: bubble yes, selection no / both yes
n log n / n log n / n²

concepts.plainText: Binary search worst case ⌈log₂(n + 1)⌉ comparisons; hash load factor α = keys/slots

items: Hash h(k) = k mod m (m prime); collisions by separate chaining or open addressing (linear, quadratic probing, double hashing).
Adjacency matrix: O(V²) space, O(1) edge test. Adjacency list: O(V + E) space. BFS uses a queue, DFS a stack or recursion; both O(V + E).
Warshall (transitive closure) O(V³). Topological sort: DFS finish order or Kahn's in-degree algorithm; only for DAGs.
Prim O(E log V) grows one tree; Kruskal O(E log E) adds cheapest safe edges (union–find). Dijkstra O((V + E) log V), no negative edges.

rows: 1NF + no partial dependency on part of a key
2NF + no transitive dependency of non-key attributes

items: Superkey ⊇ candidate key (minimal) → one chosen as primary key; a foreign key references another table's primary key.
Armstrong's axioms: reflexivity, augmentation, transitivity (+ union, decomposition, pseudo-transitivity); attribute closure X⁺ finds keys.
SQL: DDL CREATE ALTER DROP TRUNCATE; DML SELECT INSERT UPDATE DELETE; DCL GRANT REVOKE; TCL COMMIT ROLLBACK SAVEPOINT.
Relational algebra: σ selects rows, π projects columns, ⋈ joins, ∪ − ∩ set operations, × product, ρ rename, ÷ division.
Optimisation: push selections and projections down, join small results first, choose join algorithms by cost (block transfers + seeks).
ACID: atomicity (all or nothing), consistency, isolation, durability.
Anomalies: lost update, dirty read, unrepeatable read, phantom. Conflict-serializable if the precedence graph has no cycle.
Two-phase locking (growing, then shrinking) guarantees conflict serializability; strict 2PL holds exclusive locks until commit.
Deadlock prevention: wait-die (older waits, younger dies) and wound-wait (older wounds younger, younger waits).
Recovery: write-ahead logging, undo uncommitted and redo committed transactions after a crash; checkpoints limit the log scan.

concepts.plainText: Turnaround = completion − arrival; waiting = turnaround − burst time

rows: q too small → overhead, too big → FCFS

items: Critical-section solution needs mutual exclusion, progress and bounded waiting; Peterson's algorithm solves it for two processes.
Semaphore wait(S): S = S − 1, block if S < 0; signal(S): S = S + 1, wake a waiter. Binary semaphore ≈ mutex (mutex also has an owner).
Coffman deadlock conditions: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no pre-emption, circular wait — break any one to prevent deadlock.
Producer–consumer uses semaphores empty = N, full = 0 and mutex = 1; dining philosophers risks deadlock if all pick up the left fork.

concepts.latex: EAT = (1 - p)\,t_{mem} + p\,t_{fault};\qquad \text{TLB: } EAT = h(t_{tlb} + t_m) + (1 - h)(t_{tlb} + 2t_m)
concepts.plainText: Effective access time with page faults (p = fault rate) and with a TLB (h = hit ratio)

concepts.latex: \text{Logical address} = (p, d),\quad p = \left\lfloor \frac{LA}{\text{page size}} \right\rfloor,\quad d = LA \bmod \text{page size}
concepts.plainText: Page number = address ÷ page size; offset = address mod page size

items: FIFO can suffer Belady's anomaly (more frames, more faults); LRU and Optimal cannot. Optimal gives the fewest faults but needs the future.
Thrashing: too little memory per process, paging dominates; fix with the working-set model or fewer processes.
First fit, best fit, worst fit; internal fragmentation (inside a partition or page) vs external (holes between allocations).
File allocation: contiguous (fast, external fragmentation), linked (no random access), indexed/FAT/inode (random access, index overhead).

concepts.plainText: Disk access = seek time + average rotational latency (half a revolution) + transfer time

rows: nearest request next; may starve far requests
sweep to one end, then reverse
sweep one way, jump back to the start
like SCAN / C-SCAN but turn at the last request
Complete graph edges on n vertices
Linux run level for multi-user GUI (SysV)

formulas.plainText: Maximum nodes in a binary tree of height h

notes.text: Numeric questions here are mostly: postfix evaluation, tree node counts, sorting complexities, hash insert positions, Gantt-chart averages, page-fault counts for FIFO/LRU/Optimal, effective access time and disk head movement. Draw the small table each one needs before answering.
Easy swaps: preorder vs postorder; 2NF (partial) vs 3NF (transitive); wait-die vs wound-wait; internal vs external fragmentation; FIFO (can show Belady's anomaly) vs LRU (cannot).
Stability matters in tie questions: merge, insertion, bubble and radix sort are stable; quick, heap and selection sort are not.

formulas.title: Big-O definition
formulas.plainText: f(n) ≤ c·g(n) for all n ≥ n₀
formulas.description: f = O(g) when some constant multiple of g bounds f from some point on.

formulas.title: Binary-tree node bound
formulas.description: h is the height with a single root at height 0.

formulas.title: Waiting and turnaround
formulas.latex: TAT = C - A,\qquad WT = TAT - BT
formulas.plainText: TAT = completion − arrival;  WT = TAT − burst
formulas.description: Average these over all processes to compare scheduling algorithms.

formulas.title: Effective access time
formulas.description: p page-fault rate, t_m memory access time, t_f page-fault service time.

formulas.title: Disk access time
formulas.plainText: t = seek + half a rotation + bytes/transfer rate
formulas.description: rps is revolutions per second; average rotational latency is half a revolution.

flashcards.front: Which sorting algorithms run in O(n log n) in the worst case?
flashcards.back: Merge sort and heap sort (quick sort is O(n²) in the worst case).

flashcards.front: State the four Coffman conditions for deadlock.
flashcards.back: Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no pre-emption and circular wait; all four must hold for deadlock.

flashcards.front: What makes a relation BCNF but not just 3NF?
flashcards.back: In BCNF every determinant of a non-trivial FD is a superkey; 3NF also allows X → A when A is a prime attribute.

questions.questionText: With 3 frames and the reference string 1 2 3 4 1 2 5 1 2 3 4 5, FIFO page replacement causes how many page faults?
questions.explanation: FIFO faults on 1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 5, 3, 4 = 9 faults (with 4 frames it gives 10 — Belady's anomaly).

questions.questionText: A hash table of size 7 uses h(k) = k mod 7 with linear probing. After inserting 10, 17 and 24 in that order, 24 is stored in slot:
questions.explanation: 10 → slot 3; 17 → 3 taken, probe 4; 24 → 3 and 4 taken, probe 5.

questions.questionText: Processes P1, P2, P3 arrive at time 0 with bursts 24, 3 and 3 ms. The average waiting time under FCFS in the order P1, P2, P3 is:
questions.explanation: Waits are 0, 24 and 27 ms; average = 51/3 = 17 ms (SJF would give 3 ms).
